claims.statement: `langgraph.json` registers separate `reviewer` and `review-scout` graph entrypoints, which delegate to the reviewer and scout graph factories rather than the main agent graph.
The reviewer waits at most 600 seconds for a walkthrough for its target head and continues reviewing without one when the scout cannot run or finish; the scout may still store the walkthrough later.

A review scout prepares and pins the exact PR checkout, plans changed lines into walkthrough chunks, and its final middleware settles unplanned lines, stores optional human-input summary, and invalidates the PR UI.
Scout runs are head-aware: an active run for the same head is reused, a stale plan yields to a newer head, and a complete plan ends before a model call.

The reviewer graph exposes review and web-retrieval tools, while its configured tool list contains no commit, push, or PR-opening tool; its reviewer sandbox is replaceable because every run re-derives the checkout.

Reviewer and scout preparation mint repository-scoped GitHub App tokens, allow sandbox replacement, and deterministically clone-or-fetch and force-check out the requested PR head; reviewer checkout failure is best-effort while scout checkout failure terminates preparation.

Reviewer preparation builds first- or re-review diff context, reconciles existing GitHub threads, and renders untrusted PR/review-thread content with data-block escaping and bounded comment bodies before it enters the model context.
Reviewer skills are extracted from the PR base SHA to a directory outside the checkout, preventing PR-head changes to skill files from injecting reviewer instructions.
Findings are stored under a pull request in PostgreSQL with one-time migration from legacy thread metadata; evaluation runs instead use bounded in-memory run-scoped findings.
Finding mutations lock and update the freshest persisted records, merge replacements by ID, and `append_finding` deduplicates open findings by a location-and-description fingerprint.
`add_finding` validates titles, metadata, range ordering, and changed-line membership on the selected diff side; it records the live reviewer head and drops suggestions over four lines.
`publish_review` requires a complete unique ranking, posts only eligible unpublished in-diff findings, and for re-reviews restricts publication to findings first seen at the current head.

Inline review comments carry a hidden finding marker; publication records review/comment identities and reconciliation uses trusted bot markers to backfill identities, capture human replies, and resolve a finding only when all matched threads are resolved.

Publication refuses stale assessments, retries an unresolved-anchor rejection once only after pruning anchors verified against the current diff, suppresses known duplicate empty re-review summaries, and uses a metadata snapshot rather than GitHub in evaluation mode.
Resolving or dismissing a finding requires a note, and a surfaced finding is left open if GitHub review-thread resolution fails.
Both execution graphs apply preparation and bounded model/tool error middleware; the reviewer additionally refreshes its GitHub proxy, checks queued messages, and settles review checks on exit.
